# humanish

> Open-source (MIT) TypeScript CLI. Personas drive your app in a real browser on a hosted
> sandbox desktop. Runs land in your repo under `.humanish/`: screenshots, action traces,
> lifecycle events, estimated cost at dated rates. `humanish verify` grades the bundle
> fail-closed.

## When to use humanish

Reach for it when the question is "what happens when someone who is not us tries this?" and
the answer needs evidence rather than a prediction:

- a first-time visitor, a keyboard-only user, or a phone user has to get through a real flow
  (signup, first task, the thing the README promises) on a web app you maintain;
- a maintainer wants a defect report they can act on: screenshots, the participant's own words,
  a per-task funnel, a fail-closed verify grade, and a public-safe issue draft;
- a change under the UI (a probe, a prompt, a model) has to be checked against an instrument with
  known answers: `bench/` carries the planted-defect arms (58 of 60 defects reported over four
  runs, nothing invented in 15 clean runs, receipts with run ids).

Not the tool for load testing, pixel diffing, or a decision about people that needs people; the
limits page below says where simulated users diverge from real ones.

How an agent calls it: `npx humanish init --yes`, then `npx humanish run first-run` (no keys, no
spend), then `npx humanish run try-live` (a real study, capped at $2). Read results with
`npx humanish runs --json` and `npx humanish review --run latest --json`; draft feedback with
`npx humanish feedback issue --run latest`. Every command has `--json`.

## Install

```
npm i -D humanish
npx humanish init --yes
npx humanish watch
```

For coding agents: `npx skills add danielgwilson/humanish`

## Commands

Every command below exists in the shipped CLI. `tests/llms-txt-commands.test.ts` builds the
command table from the program itself and fails if this list drifts.

Getting started:

- `humanish init`: scaffold `humanish/` source files (personas, labs) and the ignored
  `.humanish/` runtime directory; `--yes` takes the defaults.
- `humanish doctor`: report project readiness and what setup is missing, including which
  provider keys were found and where. Run this first when something will not start.
- `humanish run <lab>`: run a lab. The everyday command. With no lab it renders a synthetic
  dry-run bundle locally, without keys or provider spend.
- `humanish watch`: run and keep the shell attached, with Observer open.

Authoring and inspecting labs:

- `humanish lab list`: list committed and ignored lab manifests.
- `humanish lab inspect <lab>`: read a manifest without running it.
- `humanish lab preflight <lab>`: check the manifest and target reachability before any actor
  or model spend. Run this before a first live study.
- `humanish lab run <lab>`: same as `humanish run <lab>`, grouped under `lab`.
- `humanish lab cleanup`: sweep stale provider resources left by a crashed process.

Evidence:

- `humanish verify --run latest`: grade the bundle against public-safety gates, fail-closed:
  `share_ready`, `local_only`, or `blocked`.
- `humanish review`: build a review packet from verified evidence.
- `humanish runs`: list local runs and the latest pointers.
- `humanish export --run <id>`: one self-contained `.html` of the run's Observer with screenshots inlined; refuses a bundle that is not share_ready unless `--local-only` (watermarked).
- `humanish stats`: cost, outcome, and duration roll-ups across run history (`--lab`, `--since`, `--json`); unknown costs count as unknown, never $0.
- `humanish observe`: serve a finished run's Observer over loopback instead of a file URL.
- `humanish serve`: serve the whole local run library over loopback, with optional
  tunnel-edge auth.
- `humanish cleanup`: inspect recorded resource evidence and write `cleanup.json`.
- `humanish reclaim`: kill an interrupted run's sandboxes by their journaled exact ids.

Feedback, without mutating GitHub:

- `humanish feedback draft --run latest`: generate a public-safe draft from verified evidence.
- `humanish feedback verify`: check the draft for public-issue eligibility.
- `humanish feedback issue`: print Markdown for a public issue.
- `humanish feedback issue-url`: print a prefilled issue URL.
- `humanish feedback list`: show draft state for a run.

Keys and configuration:

- `humanish keys set <provider>`: store one provider key in the user store at mode 0600,
  prompted with hidden input. `humanish keys list` prints NAMES only, never values.
  `humanish keys unset <provider>` removes one.
- `humanish telemetry status`: what is collected, and whether it is on.
  `humanish telemetry enable` and `humanish telemetry disable` change it. `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`
  also turns it off.

Other surfaces:

- `humanish tui`: the interactive terminal surface for browsing labs and runs. **This one is
  for a human, not for you.** It takes over the screen and waits for keystrokes, so it will
  refuse a non-TTY with a structured error. If you are setting humanish up on someone's behalf,
  this is the command to hand them.
- `humanish comms catch`: run the email catch on this host, to study an app that sends mail.
- `humanish codex app-server`: a Codex-native actor surface.

## Credentials

A live study needs two things in the environment:

- `E2B_API_KEY`: the hosted sandbox the persona works in. Set it with
  `npx humanish keys set e2b`, or `e2b auth login`.
- `OPENAI_API_KEY`: the model driving the persona. Set it with `npx humanish keys set openai`.
  Alternatively a signed-in local agent (Codex, Claude Code) can supply the participant, but
  `E2B_API_KEY` is still required.

`humanish doctor --json` reports which of these were found and names the exact command to fix
each missing one. Values are never printed or persisted into run artifacts.

Node 20 or newer throughout.

## Worked example: the Excalidraw study

Run `cua-2026-08-07T17-44-48-760Z-87389419` (2026-08-07): four computer-use lanes on
hosted 1920×1080 desktops drove a commit-pinned clone of Excalidraw
(excalidraw/excalidraw@4872083c), an open-source virtual whiteboard. 3/4 lanes passed;
one gave up; `humanish verify` ran 16/16 checks. Wall-clock 6m 06s; estimated cost
~$1.54 (rates as of 2026-08-05).

Lanes and verbatim outcomes:

- diagram-login-flow — persona final report: "Done"
- sticky-notes — persona final report: "Done."
- sketch-shapes — recorded reason (harness; the persona emitted no final message): "gave up: 8 consecutive turns with no change to the UI state"
- export-drawing — persona final report: "Done"

Excalidraw is the application studied; it is not a Humanish adopter or endorser.

## Guarantees (by construction)

- The actor's API key stays on your machine; the sandbox desktop never holds it.
- Evidence lands in gitignored `.humanish/`; no command publishes it.
- `humanish feedback issue` renders a draft; no GitHub API call exists on that path.
- Verify fails closed: a bundle that cannot pass every gate grades `local_only` or `blocked`, never `share_ready`.

## Known failure modes

The limits, cited: what the computer-use substrate cannot do yet, where simulated users
diverge from real ones, what a passing `humanish verify` grade does not prove, and when to
recruit real people instead. Includes first-party run ids for our own failed lanes, and
the published numbers against simulated users.

- https://humanish.dev/failure-modes

## Component registry

humanish.dev serves a shadcn-compatible component registry at `https://humanish.dev/r/<name>.json`.
Items: `humanish-tokens` (the site's token system), `terminal-cast` (static terminal
transcript), `persona-lane` (run lane with screenshot, verbatim report, honest status
chip), `pinned-replay` (the scroll-pinned run walkthrough, with the Excalidraw study's
metadata as demo data — screenshots not included).

Install directly:

```
npx shadcn@latest add https://humanish.dev/r/pinned-replay.json
```

Or configure the namespace in `components.json` and add by name:

```json
{ "registries": { "@humanish": "https://humanish.dev/r/{name}.json" } }
```

```
npx shadcn@latest add @humanish/terminal-cast
```
